evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Identify and resolve systemic data quality, modelling and pipeline issues, implementing testing, monitoring and documentation that improves trust in the data platform.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities emphasize data quality, testing, monitoring, documentation, and trust throughout with no offsetting speed/velocity language, driving a rigour classification.
evidence.domain_risk: Dispensed is building the data platform that powers clinical, commercial, and operational decisions across Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The platform powers clinical decisions for a telehealth company and the JD explicitly lists 'healthcare or regulated environments' experience as valued, meeting the high domain_risk bar for regulated healthcare.
evidence.data_team_maturity: You will help define how analytics engineering is practised at Dispensed, establishing modelling standards
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The role establishes standards and practices for an existing but still-forming analytics engineering function rather than building from zero or joining a large established team, placing it at mid.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design, build and maintain scalable data models and transformation pipelines in dbt and BigQuery, including pipeline orchestration and scheduling
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name specific tools (dbt, BigQuery), concrete deliverables (semantic models, A/B test measurement frameworks) and precise scope, consistent with hiring-manager authorship.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Partner with Product, Clinical, Commercial and Engineering teams to understand the decisions they are trying to make
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The JD names Product (product), Clinical/Commercial (commercial-adjacent healthcare), and Engineering/internal platform work with genuinely equal weight across responsibilities, giving mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: You will help define how analytics engineering is practised at Dispensed, establishing modelling standards, improving data quality, mentoring others
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role explicitly defines practice standards, mentors others, and sets strategic direction for the data platform, a clear strategic framing.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The JD contains no mention of AI tools, AI-assisted coding, or AI-consuming data infrastructure anywhere in responsibilities or requirements.
evidence.testing_framing: Identify and resolve systemic data quality, modelling and pipeline issues, implementing testing, monitoring and documentation that improves trust in the data platform.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and data quality are framed as an owned responsibility using action verbs ('identify', 'implementing'), not just a requirements-list tool mention.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Your work will determine not only what data is available, but whether it is trusted, understandable, and actionable.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust, data quality, and reliability language dominate the role summary and responsibilities section (appearing in the very first paragraph), reflecting a high loss-aversion framing centered on stakeholder trust in the data.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: This is not a role focused solely on building infrastructure or answering business questions.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The JD explicitly blends new-build work (semantic models, A/B test frameworks) with fixing existing systemic data quality and pipeline issues, giving mixed.
evidence.loss_aversion: Your work will determine not only what data is available, but whether it is trusted, understandable, and actionable — trust and reliability of data reaching clinical/commercial decision-makers is a dominant framing throughout the JD.
